Lucia, your quarterly memo landed this morning. Walk me through what actually changed.
The approval process was streamlined last quarter, and two deliverables have been completed ahead of schedule.
And the review that was flagged in March?
It was escalated to the vice president the same day, and the rationale is explained on page two.
Who owns that decision now?
The daily checks are delegated to the team leads, but the final call was made by me.
Good. And what is the rule going forward?
Every new model must be reviewed before release, so nothing is shipped without oversight. And the credit should be shared with the team.

Here is the short version of the quarter, and I will keep it to sixty seconds. The approval process was streamlined last quarter, and two full weeks were cut from the cycle. Two deliverables have been completed ahead of schedule. One issue was flagged in March. It was escalated to the vice president the same day it appeared, and the rationale for that call is explained on page two of the memo. Going forward, the rule is simple. Every new model must be reviewed before release, and nothing is shipped without oversight. The daily checks are delegated to the team leads, so the work does not sit on one desk. And the credit should be shared with the whole team, because the framework was designed by four engineers, not by one manager.

Let me give you one test before you write a single sentence. Ask yourself what the reader should notice first: the result, or the person who produced it. If the answer is the result, use the passive. The approval process was streamlined. Two deliverables have been completed. The reader sees the impact immediately, and nobody has to be named. But there is a line, and you must not cross it. When something goes wrong, the passive becomes a place to hide. Mistakes were made. You have heard that sentence, and you know exactly what is wrong with it. Nobody is named, so it sounds like cover, not precision. So here is my rule. Use the passive for results, and switch back to the active voice the moment responsibility has to be attributed to a real person. If that person is you, say so. That decision was made by me.
